 Toyota slams its Crown Signia SUV for SEMA, creates a wicked wagon 
 Modified Toyota slams its Crown Signia SUV for SEMA, creates a wicked wagon
 The Crown Signia GT-S Concept proves that sporty estates should still rule
 Greg Potts Published: 29 Oct 2026 External link to Top Gear Magazine Subscription – 3 months for £6 Skip 12 photos in the image carousel and continue reading 1 / 12 “A vehicle with room for family, friends and gear, which looks right at home carving up canyon roads.”
 That was apparently the brief for Toyota’s SEMA build this year, and so the skunkworks team at the Toyota Motorsports Garage came up with… an estate! Because if you want practicality and genuine sportiness, you don’t want an SUV.
 Advertisement - Page continues below Although, TMG did actually start with an SUV. Its creation has been christened the Crown Signia GT-S Concept, and as you can tell from the side-by-side shots up above, this build began its life as a standard 2026 Crown Signia.
 The team then chopped five inches from its ride height with custom MCS coilovers, before treating it to a wide-arched bodykit, an open-mouthed grille and a chunky rear diffuser that we’re sure is creating massive downforce.

 No word on any mechanical mods, so it’s probably still got the standard Crown Signia’s 2.5-litre four-cylinder and eCVT hybrid setup, but those gold 21in HRE wheels are surely worth an extra 100bhp.
 Anyone else reckon Toyota needs to make a wagon like this for real?
